chunks: Say: 'God gives you life, then makes you die, then will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt; but most of the people do not know.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's power over life, death, and resurrection?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Az-Zumar, this verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the cosmic cycle of life, death, and resurrection, serving as a foundational proof for the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Qiyamah). Shia exegetes often highlight the phrase 'no doubt in it' as a contrast to the skepticism of the polytheists, emphasizing that while the event is certain, human ignorance stems from a lack of reflection rather than ambiguity in divine decree. This declaration reinforces the monotheistic belief that all stages of existence are directly willed by God, a core tenet in Shia theological discussions on divine power (Qudrah).
